# Overview: Brain OS Control Base

The front page of the documentation view: what the system is, what state
it is in right now, what has shipped, and when the next update lands.
Everything on this page is OS documentation. No personal data appears here.

## Next update

<!-- NEXT-UPDATE:BEGIN (chain-maintained: updated at every increment start and finish; do not hand-edit outside the chain) -->
- **Current work:** S-KB booklet view build in slices (bundle pre-built
  2026-10-23 evening). First slice ETA Sat 2026-10-24 ~10:30 PT:
  Knowledge Base button + Overview (status, accomplishments, this
  next-update counter) live behind the existing gate. Remaining sections
  (architecture, algorithms, log feed, dictionary) follow hourly to the
  full view at the ETA below. S3 controls build is verified and
  merge-ready, held behind S-KB per the queue.
- **Next update ETA:** Sat 2026-10-24, ~14:00 PT (estimate): S-KB
  documentation view live in the portal, this bundle wired behind the
  Knowledge Base button.
- **Countdown target:** 2026-10-24T14:00:00-07:00
- **Last updated:** Fri 2026-10-23, ~20:28 PT (ETA revised by the chain).
- **Slip reason:** moved EARLIER, not slipped: the owner ordered work
  split into parallel lanes and an hourly ship cadence (2026-10-23
  ~20:17–20:21 PT), so the bundle was pre-built tonight and tomorrow's
  build is wiring only. If this ETA slips, the new time and its reason
  replace this block (ETA discipline: slippage is allowed, silence is not).
<!-- NEXT-UPDATE:END -->

## System status at a glance

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| Backend production | Complete (announced 2026-10-23 ~02:23 PT) |
| Phase 1 (Control Base) | In build. S1 sync skeleton shipped and verified 2026-10-23 |
| Live surface | Tailnet only. Public portal carries a labelled static snapshot |
| Outward window | Default OFF. One-shot, switch-gated, logged |
| Phase 1 cash spent | $0 (attempt cap: $1) |
| Next gate | G2 spec freeze, Sat 2026-10-24, 12:00 PT |

## Live counts (last recorded live payload, Fri 2026-10-23 ~19:54 PT)

Counts are system telemetry, read from the backend payload at verification
time. On the live surface these numbers flow from `/api/live-state`; on the
public surface they are the snapshot counts and are labelled as such.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Graph nodes | 799 |
| Facts in core store | ~759 (at last sealing, 2026-10-23) |
| Relations | ~1,446 (at last sealing, 2026-10-23) |
| Current beat | 716 |
| Inbox waiting at the gate | 240 |
| Open demands in payload | 1 |
| Graph history | Beats 97 to 597 backfilled; genesis beat 97 held 574 nodes |

## Recent accomplishments (glance)

- **2026-10-23:** S1 sync skeleton shipped: vitals strip and freshness
  guard wired to the live backend, 10 of 10 acceptance tests green,
  merged to master (commit 516c53b, repair 2c8c0a2), rollback tag set.
- **2026-10-23:** Brain OS Control Base chartered; Phase 1 plan, Law 0,
  and quality bars recorded; S0 research completed (13 sources).
- **2026-10-23:** Backend production completed and announced with full
  inventory (write-gate, consolidate, Local Max ask endpoint, outward
  window, graph history, OCR sense path, doorbell relay).
- Full list with dates and tags: see `accomplishments.md`.

## How this view stays true

- The view is **auto-managed**: it renders this bundle, and the bundle is
  regenerated from source files by the portal-sync pipeline. Nobody
  hand-edits the view.
- **Law 0** governs the whole product: visual state equals data state,
  live, with a ~1 second staleness bound on the tailnet surface. The UI
  displays its own sync age; if the feed dies, the brain visibly sleeps.
- The view sits behind the portal's existing password and TOTP gate. No
  new auth surface was added for it.

sections.title: Architecture: Brain OS Control Base
sections.body:
# Architecture: Brain OS Control Base

The system in one page: what the parts are, how information moves, and
where the boundaries sit. All mechanisms named here are implemented in
the brain repo at `~/workspace/company/dream-brain/`; file paths are
given so any claim can be checked against the code.

## The two halves: mind and body

| Half | Where it lives | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| The BRAIN (mind) | The owner's home machine (WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04), brain home `/root/brain` | The living system: backend, memory stores, nightly consolidation, senses |
| The BODY | GitHub repo `dream-brain` (master) | Ingestion, durable storage, publishing, the immune system (gates and tests) |

One product, two halves. The repo on this machine
(`~/workspace/company/dream-brain/`, with a bridge copy at
`~/workspace/brain-bridge/dream-brain/`) is the working tree the build
chain operates on.

## Core components

| Component | Location | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Core store | `core/` (`facts.jsonl`, `relations.jsonl`, `constitution.md`, `identity.md`) | The brain's self: identity-bearing, slow-changing memory |
| Knowledge pages | `knowledge/` (people, projects, topics, places, patterns, library) | Nodes that facts attach to; the graph the portal renders |
| Inbox pipeline | `inbox/` (raw, proposals, processed, rejected, held) | Every arrival lands here first, as a claim, never as a fact |
| Scripts (the machinery) | `scripts/` (Node.js, zero or near-zero dependencies) | Gates, scorers, consolidation, sync, senses: see `algorithms.md` |
| Portal (the face) | `portal/` (`app.js`, `universe.js`, `vitals.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css`) | The control base UI: living graph, vitals strip, and this documentation view |
| Local Max | `local-max/` + `scripts/local-max-ask.mjs` | The on-box ask endpoint (`/api/ask`): answers from the fact corpus with citations |
| Backend service | Box: `/root/brain/backend/server.mjs` (systemd `brain-backend`, 127.0.0.1:3000) | Serves `/api/live-state` and the SSE stream `/api/stream`; accepts the write-only `/api/doorbell` intake |

## How information moves

**In (the senses).** A capture arrives (phone Shortcut, chat, issue) and
rings the doorbell (`scripts/doorbell.mjs`): notice only, exactly once.
The item lands in the inbox as RAW material. Intake processing turns it
into candidate claims. Nothing enters memory directly.

**Through the membrane (the write-gate).** Every candidate passes the
deterministic write-gate (`scripts/write-gate.mjs`): specificity,
valid-from, source, relations. Passing candidates merge as facts;
failures bounce to triage and are never silently dropped. A batch
hard-stop (50 facts) and human approval tokens bound every merge.

**Sleep (consolidate).** Nightly, `scripts/consolidate.mjs` runs its 11
steps: collect, validate, merge, index, curate, report, commit, push,
doctor, revert-on-failure, summary. This is the visible sleep cycle in
the sync map: the brain dims while it consolidates.

**Growth (rewire and history).** Relations are proposed, agreed, and
drawn in; usage thickens exercised relations (plasticity). Every sync
beat appends to the append-only graph history
(`scripts/graph-history.mjs`, `portal/graph-history.jsonl`), which the
growth slider later scrubs.

**Out (the face).** The box backend publishes live state at
`/api/live-state` and streams changes over SSE at `/api/stream`.
Tailscale Serve maps the tailnet URL to the backend. The portal reads
the state and renders it; the public site receives only an encrypted
static snapshot through the portal-sync publish pipeline.

## The two views (never merged)

| View | For whom | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Human view | The owner | The living being: graph, flowing vitals, demands in plain words, this documentation |
| Operator view | Max | Data and pipelines: what is green, what is stuck, seat and sync health |

Both render the same `/api/live-state` truth. They are two renderings of
one state, not two states.

## Access and safety boundaries

- **Consent gate.** The brain accepts only whom the owner grants:
  portal password plus TOTP (live since 2026-10-08), live data
  tailnet-only, public surface is a static snapshot. Phase 1 changed no
  auth and added no inbound surface.
- **Egress discipline.** Code-level classification (`scripts/classify.mjs`)
  decides what may leave the machine and to which sink. The outward
  window is the only web pull path: default OFF, one-shot, bounded,
  results staged RAW outside the membrane.
- **Fail-closed gates.** Every gate in the system refuses on error
  rather than guessing: write-gate, eval-gate, promotion-gate,
  selfmod-guard. Prompts suggest; gates enforce.
- **Kill switches.** `BRAIN_WRITES=0` forces read-only mode;
  `BRAIN_CRONS=0` refuses cron-triggered mutations. Invalid values are
  refused, never defaulted open.

## The OS domain (seeded, scene S-OS, after S3)

A registry through which the brain talks to its own OS: demands,
settings, and controls as first-class registered objects. The brain may
register a new control (a dial for one of its own parameters) and surface
it in the UI; the owner sets the range and the locks, and turns the
dial. Design-changing registrations cross the existing approval split
and the self-modification guard (`scripts/selfmod-guard.mjs`). Chartered
2026-10-23; specced as its own handout after S3 controls ship.

sections.title: Algorithms and Methods
sections.body:
# Algorithms and Methods

Every mechanism the OS runs, described as implemented. Each section
names its source file in the brain repo (`~/workspace/company/dream-brain/`)
so the description can be checked against the code. A design rule runs
through all of them: deterministic first. Where a model is used at all,
it is local, on the box, and a deterministic algorithm makes the final
call.

## 1. The write-gate: what may become a fact

- **Source:** `scripts/write-gate.mjs` (version `write-gate/v1`)
- **Job:** deterministic admission gate for fact candidates. Local-only,
  zero-dependency, no model, no network.
- **Four checks, in fixed order:**
  1. **Specificity.** The candidate text is scored against a hedge-word
     lexicon (vague words and phrases such as "maybe", "various",
     "stuff", "many things"). Minimum passing score: 0.30
     (`SPECIFICITY_MIN`). Multi-word phrases match first so a phrase is
     counted once.
  2. **Valid-from.** Every fact carries a validity stamp and a precision
     (day, month, year, unknown). Unknown precision passes only for
     atemporal relation types (INSTANCE, COMPONENT, CONTRADICTS,
     CHALLENGES, EXTENDS, REFINES).
  3. **Source.** The source reference must match a strict path pattern,
     or the `external:` form. Unverifiable sources fail.
  4. **Relations.** Declared relations must resolve to real targets in
     the typed relation vocabulary.
- **Failure handling:** failures bounce to `inbox/triage/<id>.triage.json`.
  Nothing is dropped and nothing is auto-deleted; retention is indefinite.
- **Fail-closed mode:** the gate mode resolves from the `WRITE_GATE`
  environment value; any value other than the recognised ones refuses
  (exit 2) rather than defaulting open.
- **Enforcement points:** intake processing and the brain merge. The gate
  is code, not a prompt instruction: prompts suggest, gates enforce.

## 2. Surprise scoring: what the brain wants to know next

- **Source:** `scripts/surprise-v2.mjs` (version 1.0.0), with the gravity
  floor reproduced from `scripts/core-gravity.mjs`
- **Job:** information-gain ranking of open demand proposals, so the
  brain works on what would teach it the most.
- **Two scores per demand:**
  - **Legacy score** (authoritative today): the gravity ranking the core
    already uses, reproduced per-fact with a floor of 0.10, then max.
  - **V2 score** (experimental): (severity x centrality) + novelty, with
    each component normalised independently. Severity saturates at 3
    distinct contradiction involvements. V2 becomes the sort key only
    if it wins the seeded benchmark; until then legacy rules.
- **Anomaly detection (SEKA-lite):** 2-hop path-pattern analysis over
  new and changed relation edges (edges younger than 30 days). A path
  signature is "dominant" for an edge type when it covers at least 15%
  of that type's edges and at least 5 edges in absolute terms. A new
  edge whose path signature diverges (Jaccard threshold 0.5) is flagged
  as a pattern-breaking anomaly and staged as a proposal.
- **Invariants:** writes only to `.brain/surprise-scores.jsonl`,
  `.brain/seka-anomalies.jsonl`, and anomaly proposals in
  `inbox/proposals/`. Zero model calls, zero network. The scorer reads
  only id, evidence, status, kind, class, and created-at fields from
  demand rows, never their statement text. Fully deterministic: same
  inputs, same rows.

## 3. Core gravity: what pulls toward the centre

- **Source:** `scripts/core-gravity.mjs`
- **Job:** score how strongly each node in the mesh pulls toward the
  centre of the mind. Runs on every heartbeat think-beat and nightly
  before consolidation. Pure signal aggregation: zero dependencies, no
  model calls.
- **Formula (v1):**
  `w = min(1, 0.10 + 0.25 x echo_freq + 0.25 x demand_refs + 0.20 x recency + 0.20 x degree)`
  Nodes named in contradictions or dangling wires are multiplied by 1.5
  (capped at 1.0). Norms are min-max over the mesh. Missing inputs
  degrade to the 0.10 base.
- **Output:** `.brain/gravity.json`, written atomically.
- **Visible consequence (the 0.8 rule):** a node whose confidence
  reaches 0.8 or above earns a direct core link and migrates inward in
  the UI, keeping all its previous links. New nodes are born at the
  edge and migrate only when the core has refined them.

## 4. Consolidate: the sleep cycle

- **Source:** `scripts/consolidate.mjs`
- **Job:** the nightly mechanical consolidation. The model step runs
  before it and may only add new files to `inbox/` and `reports/`; this
  script validates, merges, doctors, and pushes. Zero dependencies.
- **The 11 steps, in order:** collect, validate, merge, index, curate,
  report, commit, push, doctor, revert-on-failure, summary.
- **Safety switches (fail-closed):** `BRAIN_CRONS=0` refuses all
  cron-triggered mutations; `BRAIN_WRITES=0` forces read-only mode
  (validate and report only, refusals recorded in the run report, never
  silent). Any value other than 0 or 1 refuses the run.
- **Housekeeping constants:** zombie threshold 60 days; the hot summary
  file is capped at 500 words; push retries up to 3 attempts; page-size
  budgets enforced per knowledge directory.
- **Failure handling:** a failure writes an alarm to `reports/` and the
  revert-on-failure step restores the tree; alarms are never silent.

## 5. Calibration: does the brain know how sure it is (KP2)

- **Source:** `scripts/calibration-tracker.mjs` (version 1.0.0)
- **Job:** every confidence the brain assigns is recorded as a
  prediction. Each prediction resolves against a deterministic external
  outcome, never against the brain judging itself. Hit-rate per
  confidence bin produces a correction curve in `.brain/calibration.json`.
- **Rules:** raw confidence is never modified anywhere; the curve is a
  separate file. Look-ahead is banned (a prediction whose outcome is
  already decided at track time is never tracked). Outcome rows are
  ground truth 0 or 1 only; "abstain" is rejected by design, so stale
  predictions stay open rather than being resolved by guesswork.
  History is append-only and never rewritten.

## 6. Boundary probe: mapping known, shaky, unknown (KP1)

- **Source:** `scripts/boundary-probe.mjs` (version 1.0.0)
- **Method:** discrete semantic entropy (Kuhn et al. 2023). Each open
  question is asked 5 times of the box-local model (qwen2.5:1.5b via
  Ollama on loopback). The answers are clustered by meaning with a
  deterministic algorithm; the entropy across clusters tags the
  question known, shaky, or unknown-zone.
- **Consequence:** unknown-zone questions stage a demand proposal
  through the proposal convention. The probe never writes demands
  directly; the demand auto-gate decides.
- **Privacy invariants:** the only network destination is loopback
  (127.0.0.1:11434); any other destination is refused. Sensitive content
  tiers are refused from every non-local sink: such questions are
  skipped and counted, never sent. Model failure never writes partial
  state.

## 7. Verdict ledger: judging proposals without self-deception (KP3)

- **Source:** `scripts/verdict-ledger.mjs`
- **Method:** the Reflexion pattern (Shinn et al. 2023) with a
  deterministic external evaluator: proposal (actor), rule-based verdict
  (evaluator), a 1 to 2 sentence templated reflection, and the ledger
  itself as episodic memory (`.brain/verdict-ledger.jsonl`, append-only).
- **Boundary rule:** the evaluator never reads reflection text. Ledger
  rows are field-stripped on load, so no reasoning narrative can leak
  back into evaluation. Matching is regex-exact on fact-id tokens, no
  fuzzy matching.
- **Fail-closed:** a corrupt ledger or input refuses with zero writes.
  Same-day re-runs are idempotent.

## 8. Prediction engine: saying what happens next, then scoring it

- **Source:** `scripts/prediction-engine.mjs`
- **Job:** for key nodes (top degree centrality plus configured
  interests), generate 2 to 3 scenario rows (baseline, favorable,
  adverse), each with a predicted outcome, contributing factors with a
  weight and confidence per factor, and a time horizon.
- **Scoring:** resolution compares scenarios against deterministic
  ground truth (hit, miss, expired). Misses append to the prediction
  mistake bank. Reports include hit-rate, Brier scores, and an ASCII
  calibration table.
- **Standing:** predictions are advisory only. They never enter the
  proposal pipeline and no daemon consumes them automatically.

## 9. Promotion gate: what may rise into the core

- **Source:** `scripts/promotion-gate.mjs`
- **Job:** the hard gate a fact must pass to be promoted to identity
  level. Local-only, no model calls, writes nothing to `knowledge/`.
- **Criteria, first match wins, fixed order:**
  - **G2, direct confirmation:** a session-log approval naming the fact,
    or identity permanence tier of 0.9 or above.
  - **G1, two or more independent sightings:** distinct (channel, date)
    pairs across captures, proposals, demand-question references, and
    session-log lines. The system's own echoes never count.
  - **G3, corroborating source:** a cross-verify verdict of
    "corroborated", and only that verdict.
- **Relation upgrades** of causal types additionally require the owner's
  promote token; the check throws (fail-closed) without it.

## 10. Graph history: the memory of growth

- **Source:** `scripts/graph-history.mjs`; data at
  `portal/graph-history.jsonl`
- **Job:** append-only birth log of the graph at sync beats. Rows carry
  fact ids, beats, timestamps, and counts only, never labels or fact
  text, so the history file is safe to publish with the portal.
- **Backfill:** history was reconstructed across beats 97 to 597;
  genesis beat 97 held 574 nodes. Capture appends to the working tree
  and never commits; the portal-sync commit stages the file.
- **Visible consequence:** the growth slider scrubs this history at
  10-beat adaptive steps (it slides; it never rotates).

## 11. The doorbell: exactly-once notice of arrivals

- **Source:** `scripts/doorbell.mjs`
- **Job:** watch the detection streams (inbox watch, fastpoll relay) and
  ring once for every new detection, immediately. Notice only: the
  doorbell never moves, parses, or processes files.
- **Exactly-once method:** every detection line is hashed (sha12). A
  marker file is written atomically BEFORE the event is emitted, so a
  restart sees the marker and skips: duplicates are impossible, and the
  worst crash case is at-most-once emission with the marker itself
  holding the full event for audit. Markers older than 30 days are
  pruned at the end of each run.
- **Fanout:** a best-effort POST to the backend's write-only
  `/api/doorbell` intake, which fans out to SSE. A network failure is
  recorded on the event and never breaks the run.

## 12. The live sync mechanism, and Law 0 as implemented

- **Sources:** box backend `/root/brain/backend/server.mjs` (systemd
  `brain-backend`); portal reader `portal/vitals.js` with the additive
  `window.__brainVitals` export in `portal/app.js` (shipped in S1,
  commit 2c8c0a2).
- **Transport:** the backend serves current state at `/api/live-state`
  and streams changes over Server-Sent Events at `/api/stream`.
  Tailscale Serve maps the tailnet URL to the backend. Live data never
  leaves the tailnet; the public portal receives a static snapshot.
- **Law 0 (the rule):** visual state equals data state, live. The
  Phase 1 staleness bound is about 1 second on tailnet. The UI shows
  its own sync age; it never hides it.
- **The reader (S1):** `vitals.js` reads only through
  `window.__brainVitals.read()` on a 250 ms requestAnimationFrame loop.
  It opens no listeners on the feed and makes no network calls. Digits
  roll with compositor-only transforms; only changed digit columns
  animate.
- **The freshness guard:** sync age is computed from the newest of the
  state timestamp, the sync timestamp, and the last local contact time.
  If contact is lost for 60 seconds, and only while the portal is
  unlocked, the brain visibly sleeps (a `.sleeping` state on the
  universe and graph elements) and the age counter keeps climbing. The
  mirror never pretends to be live when it is not.
- **Gate test:** at G3, and re-run at G4 and G5, one real fact is
  changed in the backend by hand and the UI must move, timed, in front
  of witnesses (the kill-the-feed test).

## 13. The outward window: bounded sight, RAW staging only

- **Source:** `scripts/window-pull.mjs`
- **Job:** data-in only. Pulls public factual text for approved demands
  and unknown-zone questions, and stages it as RAW inbox items for the
  normal intake machinery. Nothing is written to knowledge pages.
- **Bounds per run:** at most 20 fetches; 15 second timeout per fetch;
  500 KB maximum per fetch; 2 second gap between fetches; at most 10
  claims staged per pull.
- **Egress discipline:** the source item must pass the egress classifier
  for the public-web sink. Queries are built from a strict
  capitalised-entity whitelist with a name blocklist. Hosts are the
  pinned Tier-1 allowlist, or Tier-2 hosts carrying a scope approval
  record. Default state of the window: OFF.

## 14. Skills admission: how the brain learns a new skill safely

- **Source:** `scripts/skill-admission.mjs`
- **Pipeline:** VERIFY (frontmatter gate, reserved keys, slug collision,
  static scan, advisory de-duplication, classification), then SANDBOX
  (isolated first run of declared tests, a tree-escape invariant, a
  usefulness gate for prompt-only skills), then ADMIT (freshness and
  hash binding, approval token required for script skills, install via
  the skill registry), then CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT (usage votes,
  periodic re-tests, retirement of skills that stop earning their keep).
- **Boundary:** local-only; the only model call is the box-local
  usefulness judge on loopback. Skill content never leaves the box.

## 15. Local Max ask: retrieval with citations

- **Source:** `local-max/ask/v1/ask.mjs` (the canonical bundle; the shipped box library). `scripts/local-max-ask.mjs` is now only the bundle build/check tool.
- **Job:** `POST /api/ask` answers questions from the brain's fact
  corpus and cites fact ids. Check order inside the handler: parse,
  concurrency mutex, rate limit, seat decision, identity, freshness,
  history, retrieval, think, citations, chat-log append. Authentication
  runs before all of it, so an unauthenticated caller can never hold
  the mutex or consume a rate slot.
- **Seat rule:** an external model seat is used only when the request
  explicitly asks for it, the seat-enabled switch file exists, the
  daily cap is not reached, and the caller passed auth. A seat request
  with the switch absent is refused, never silently downgraded. Only a
  person pressing a button in a UI may request the seat; no scheduler
  may.

## 16. Self-modification guard: the brain may not rewrite itself freely

- **Source:** `scripts/selfmod-guard.mjs`
- **Job:** process gate answering one question: may this
  self-modification land? Changes to the brain's own machinery
  (`scripts/`, `config/`, `core/`) are allowed only on a feature branch.
  Merging to master requires a council approval token bound to the
  branch name and its tree hash, fail-closed on any drift. Package
  installs are checked against a pinned allowlist.
- **Enforcement:** a pre-push git hook, a coordinator check before any
  merge of a self-modification branch, and the token verification at
  merge. The guard is read-only over content; its only writes are
  refusal rows in its own log.

## 17. Eval gate: quality that blocks, not reports

- **Source:** `scripts/eval-gate.mjs`, runner `scripts/eval-v0.mjs`
- **Job:** run the evaluation suite against the brain root and compare
  with the recorded baseline (`.brain/eval/baseline.json`). The gate
  fails closed: exit 1 if the score falls below the 35 of 38 floor,
  below the baseline, shows any new failure against the baseline, or
  contains any false memory. On failure the sync workflow aborts: the
  merge is reset, no tag, no push, no publish.

sections.title: Tech Stack
sections.body:
# Tech Stack

What the OS is built from. The stack is deliberately small: plain files,
deterministic scripts, and the platform the owner already runs. Free
paths and subscription seats only; Phase 1 cash budget is $1 total.

## Runtime and languages

| Layer | Technology | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Brain machinery | Node.js (ES modules, `.mjs`) | Zero or near-zero dependencies by design; Node built-ins preferred |
| Portal UI | Plain JavaScript, HTML, CSS | `portal/app.js`, `portal/universe.js`, `portal/vitals.js`; no framework, no build step |
| Graph rendering | Canvas-based renderer in `portal/universe.js` | UI-2.1 renderer, owner-accepted; reused, not replaced |
| Data formats | JSON, JSONL, Markdown | Facts and relations as JSONL; knowledge pages and all documentation as Markdown |
| Version control | Git + GitHub | Master is the durable body; feature branches for builds; rollback tags per scene |

## The brain box

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Machine | Owner's home machine, Windows 11 Pro host |
| Brain environment | WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04 |
| Backend service | Node HTTP service, systemd unit `brain-backend`, bound to 127.0.0.1:3000 |
| Endpoints | `GET /api/live-state`, `GET /api/stream` (SSE), `POST /api/doorbell` (write-only intake) |
| Local model | Ollama on loopback (127.0.0.1:11434), qwen2.5:1.5b for boundary probing and on-box judging |
| OCR sense | Tesseract 5.3.4 (screen text path, `scripts/screen-ocr.mjs`) |

## Networking and access

| Path | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Live surface | Tailscale Serve: the machine's tailnet URL maps `/api` to the local backend. Tailnet-only |
| VM to box | SSH over the Tailscale proxy path; root-owned brain paths read as the WSL root user |
| Public surface | GitHub Pages: encrypted static snapshot of the portal, published by the portal-sync pipeline |
| Portal gate | Password plus TOTP (WebAuthn-style MFA flow in the portal envelope, live since 2026-10-08) |

## Pipelines and scheduling

| Job | Mechanism | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| Build driver | Scheduled agent chain (plan, review, build, verify) | Every 30 minutes |
| Brain bridge relay | Shell relay, VM to box inbox, hash-verified | Every 15 minutes |
| Consolidate | `scripts/consolidate.mjs` on the box | Nightly |
| Portal sync | Publish pipeline (snapshot capture, graph history append, encrypt, push) | On master change |
| Watch daemons | Doorbell watch, inbox watch, relay fastpoll | Continuous, 30 second sweeps |

## Worker seats (the dev house)

Dispatch is by scene, not by project: each kind of work goes to the seat
that holds the right tool.

| Seat | Used for |
|---|---|
| Max (manager) | Plans, handouts, verification, merge and ship decisions |
| Claude Code CLI | Code builds, in isolated worktrees, Sonnet model |
| Claude chat | Deep review of plans (announced before use, one project only) |
| Gemini Spark | Delegated research and Google-side tasks (owner's account only) |
| API seats | Cheap single-turn words: Claude Haiku, Gemini Flash-Lite |

## Lightweight budgets (Phase 1, binding)

- Reuse the UI-2.1 renderer; no new heavy library without a written
  reason in the scene handout.
- Ambient particle budget capped; frame time measured on phone-class
  hardware at gate G3.
- The vitals reader polls a local export at 250 ms and animates with
  compositor-only transforms; it opens no extra network connections.
- Every brain script runs offline by default; the only network paths
  are loopback, the tailnet, and the gated outward window.

sections.title: Plan and Gates: Phase 1
sections.body:
# Plan and Gates: Phase 1

Project: **Brain OS Control Base** (seed name: NeuralGlance UI OS).
Chartered 2026-10-23. Owner: Vibhu. Manager: Max.
Full plan: `files/control-base-phase1-plan-2026-10-23.md`.
Charter and risks: `~/memory/company/projects/brain-os-control-base/`.

## What Phase 1 is

A control base over the living brain: a glass-screen OS layer through
which the brain is seen, governed, and spoken to. The brain and its
nodes are the product; the OS, the UI, and this documentation are its
mirror and instruments.

Three founding truths:

1. **The brain must see itself before it can think.** The UI is its
   mirror; its self-view is 360 degrees, wider than the human view.
2. **Two views, never merged.** The owner's human living view, and
   Max's operator view of data and pipelines. Same truth, two renderings.
3. **Sync runs through the senses.** The phone is the brain's sense
   organ (eyes, ears, mouth). The work is teaching the brain to process
   what its senses bring, not manufacturing data input.

## Law 0 (above every other rule in this plan)

Visual state equals data state, live, real time. Transport is the SSE
stream. Staleness bound on tailnet: about 1 second, measured at every
gate. The UI displays its own sync age; if the feed dies, the brain
visibly sleeps. The public snapshot keeps its own honest bound and is
labelled a snapshot.

## Scenes (the work breakdown)

| Scene | Content | Done condition (short form) |
|---|---|---|
| S0 Research | How the best builders make data feel alive; methods only | Reference sheet filed; motion language picked per sync-map row |
| S1 Sync skeleton | Vitals strip from `/api/live-state`; flowing numbers; freshness guard | Build green; kill-feed test passes; 5 spot checks by hand. **Shipped 2026-10-23** |
| S-KB Booklet view | This documentation view behind one Knowledge Base button; auto-managed bundle | View live; bundle regenerates from sources; next-update counter running |
| S2 Formation | Node birth, ghost-until-validated, relation draw-in (~900 ms), overlay budget 24 | Spec checklist green; hover never re-seeds ambient flow |
| S3 Controls | Plain-words Settings; outward-window switch on the real flag (default OFF); gate queue; Needs-You demands | Every switch provably flips real backend state, twice |
| S4 Brain bar | Ask Local Max in the portal; thinking nodes light from the real retrieval set; citations | 5 test questions return cited answers; lit nodes match citation set |
| S5 Slider + sleep face | Growth slider over graph history (slides, never rotates); consolidate dimming; morning after-glow | Slider scrubs genesis to now without jank at phone class; one real consolidate seen sleeping (or a labelled replay) |
| S6 Voice loop, minimal | iOS dictation into the ask bar; answers spoken by the phone's built-in speech, on-device | Owner asks one question by voice at the check and hears the answer |
| S7 Proof + ship | Security diff audit, performance pass, rollback tag, publish via portal-sync | Verification report filed; the live link is what the owner opens at the check |

Cut order under pressure: S6 is the first cut candidate. S-KB is
protected: it is the owner's direction-giving surface.

## Control parity (Addendum 3, binding on S1 to S3)

One control set on every device. Every action available by touch is
available by mouse, touchpad, and keyboard: tap, drag, pinch, and
long-press mirrored by click, drag, wheel, and two-finger gestures. The
keyboard set is space-explorer style: arrows or WASD fly, Q/E or +/-
zoom, F focuses the selected node, Enter opens, Esc returns, Tab walks
nodes in relation order, ? shows the key map. Boundary, in the owner's
words: this is not a game. No scores, levels, rewards, or play loops.
Every interaction either shows truth or governs the brain.

## Gates

| Gate | When (PT) | What passes it |
|---|---|---|
| G1 Plan pass | Fri 2026-10-23 | Plan plus charter; owner's GO. **Given 2026-10-23 ~19:02** |
| G2 Spec freeze | Sat 2026-10-24, 12:00 | Every sync-map row specified or cut |
| G3 Build green | Sun 2026-10-25, 12:00 | All done conditions verified; performance measured; kill-feed test passed; cut list, if any, announced before the check |
| G4 Prototype check | Sun 2026-10-25, 19:00 | Owner's live acceptance on his iPhone, including one Shortcut capture arriving live and one spoken question answered aloud, plus keyboard-only and touch-only passes |
| G5 Qualify | Mon 2026-10-26, 07:00 | The six charter criteria checked one by one, with receipts |
| The month marker | Mon 2026-11-23 | The owner's prophecy deadline for what Max becomes |

Pre-check ritual: Sun 2026-10-25, 18:30 PT (daemons verified, relay
proven, box heartbeat fresh).

## Constraints

- **Budget:** $1 cash maximum for the whole Phase 1 attempt.
  Subscription seats and free paths only. Spent so far: $0.
- **Security:** frozen. No auth change, no new inbound surface, no data
  to third parties. Live data tailnet-only; public is a static snapshot.
- **Quality bars (owner):** as light as light, as optimised as
  optimised, as premium as premium; the UI must be beautiful. At G4 the
  owner's eye outranks every metric.

## ETA discipline (owner, 2026-10-23)

Every increment publishes an ETA, labelled as an estimate. Slippage is
allowed; silence is not. When work extends, the new time is printed with
its reason. The Overview page of this view carries the live
"Next update in" counter, fed by the chain-maintained status block.

## Phase 2 seeds (recorded, not started)

Full voice (the brain speaks in its own voice, LM-4); the brain's
self-imagination surface; operator-view expansion; the OS domain
registry (scene S-OS, chartered 2026-10-23, specced after S3); service
documentation for others, only on the owner's word and only when the
product deserves it.

sections.title: Dictionary
sections.body:
# Dictionary

The words this OS uses, each with one definition. When a document uses
a different word for the same thing, the document changes, not the term.
Sources: the Booklet, Part 8, and the brain repo glossary (`GLOSSARY.md`).

## System terms

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Beat | One heartbeat cycle of the brain; also one recorded moment of graph history, the unit the growth slider steps through |
| Boundary probe (KP1) | The brain asking itself its open questions repeatedly (5 samples, semantic entropy) to map known, shaky, and unknown; unknowns become demand proposals |
| Brain | The whole system: repo, scripts, schedules, portal. The mind; GitHub is the body |
| Brain bar | The ask surface (Local Max) inside the control base |
| Calibration (KP2) | Binning the brain's confidence scores and tracking hit-rate per bin, so stated confidence can be corrected against outcomes |
| Capture | One item arriving through the doorbell intake |
| Claim | An unaccepted assertion: an inbox proposal not yet through the gate. Claims are never quoted as facts |
| Consolidate | The nightly mechanical job: inbox proposals validated, merged, indexed, reported, committed, pushed, doctored |
| Control base | The OS layer over the brain: glass screen, two views, consent gate. Seed name: NeuralGlance UI OS |
| Core | The identity-bearing centre: the `core/` files plus promoted memory. The brain's self; stable, slow-changing |
| Demand | A work item the brain raises for itself or the dev house, from a gap it found. Tracked, budgeted, closed with evidence |
| Doorbell | The capture intake that rings when something arrives: notice only, exactly-once, never processes the item itself |
| Fact | One accepted, evidence-backed line in the core store, with source, confidence, and validity window |
| Gate | Deterministic code that allows or refuses an action. Gates fail closed. Prompts suggest; gates enforce |
| Ghost | A node shown translucent until the write-gate validates it: proposed, not yet true |
| Graph history | The append-only birth log of the graph at sync beats; ids, beats, timestamps, counts only |
| Law 0 | Visual state equals data state, live, real time; the UI shows its own sync age and visibly sleeps when the feed dies |
| Local Max | The on-box ask endpoint (`/api/ask`): answers from the fact corpus, with citations |
| Membrane | The brain's surface where arrivals wait as ghosts until the gate admits them |
| Needs-You | Demands only the owner can answer; shown amber in his view |
| Node | A page in `knowledge/` that facts attach to, and its rendering in the graph |
| Outward window | The brain's bounded web sight: default OFF, one-shot, switch-gated, logged, results staged RAW |
| Portal | The visualisation surface. A permission-filtered projection of the graph for viewing: not the store, not the truth |
| Relation | A typed link between facts, from the fixed relation vocabulary |
| Seat | A capability slot in the dev house (a worker identity with a budget and an owner) |
| Skill | A playbook the brain or an agent reads at run time. Safety lives in code, never in a skill |
| Surprise | The information-gain score that orders the demand queue: what would teach the brain the most |
| Sync age | Seconds since the UI's last live event. Displayed, never hidden |
| Verdict ledger (KP3) | The append-only record of deterministic proposal verdicts, each with a short reflection the evaluator never reads |
| Write-gate | The deterministic judgment checkpoint every fact candidate passes before it becomes knowledge |

## Project terms

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Circuit breaker | 2 failed rounds on one blocker: change approach or reassign; never grind a third |
| Gate (G1 to G5) | A decision checkpoint in Phase 1: plan pass, spec freeze, build green, owner live acceptance, qualify |
| Handout | The written work order every seat needs before starting: plan section, scope fence, done condition, checks |
| Peak live smartness | The owner's shorthand for the whole build: the smartest the brain can be, alive, in real time, with no limit to its learning |
| Plasticity | Relations strengthening with use, drawn thicker in the owner's view |
| Scene (S0 to S7, S-KB, S-OS) | One work-breakdown unit of the build, with one owner and one done condition |
| Wajah rule | Every delay gets its reason, stated plainly, with a new time. Applied to ETAs by the ETA discipline |

sections.title: Log Feed
sections.body:
# Log Feed

The running record of system operations and library changes, newest
first. This feed documents the OS and its build. It contains no personal
data.

## Format contract (for the generator)

- One entry per event. Each entry is a single line:
  `- **YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM PT** [SOURCE] Event in one factual sentence.`
- Sources: `[KB]` for knowledge base library changes (from
  `knowledge-base/LOG.md`), `[OPS]` for brain build and operations
  events (from `dream-brain/knowledge/patterns/ops-log.md`).
- Newest first, always. Times in America/Vancouver.
- **Repetitive routine entries are never silently dropped.** Routine
  sweeps (watch checks, heartbeats, relay confirmations) are collapsed
  into one pattern line with a count, for example:
  `[OPS] Watch checks: 24 runs today, all steady state, 0 failures.`
  The raw entries remain one tap away in the source logs.
- An entry is written when it happens, by the chain that did the work.
  The feed is append-only; corrections are new entries, never edits.

## Latest entries

sections.title: Docs Bundle Manifest: Brain OS Control Base, Documentation View (S-KB)
sections.body:
# Docs Bundle Manifest: Brain OS Control Base, Documentation View (S-KB)

**Purpose.** This bundle is the content layer of the Knowledge Base view
(scene S-KB) inside the brain's portal UI. The view is wiring; this bundle
is the writing. Every section is generated from named source files so the
portal-sync pipeline can regenerate the bundle without hand-edited
duplicate copy.

**Scope law (owner, 2026-10-23 19:44 PT, hard).** This bundle documents
the OPERATING SYSTEM only: architecture, tech stack, algorithms, methods,
pipelines, plan and gates, system status counts, build log, accomplishments,
and project doctrine. The owner's personal data (facts about his life,
people, private lane content) never enters this bundle, in any section,
on any surface. System counts and telemetry are OS documentation and are
allowed.

**Generation rule.** Edit the source, never the bundle. On each portal-sync
run, each section below is rebuilt from its listed sources. The only
hand-maintained record inside the bundle is the NEXT-UPDATE block in
`overview.md`, which the build chain updates at every increment start and
finish (ETA discipline, plan Addendum 2).

## Sections

| # | File | Section in view | Generated from (sources) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `overview.md` | Overview | `knowledge-base/STATE-OF-THE-BUILD-*.md` (latest), `knowledge-base/REFERENCE.md`, live-state counts from the box backend (`/api/live-state`, snapshot copy at `dream-brain/portal/live-state.json`), chain-maintained NEXT-UPDATE block (in-file) |
| 2 | `architecture.md` | Architecture | `files/backend-ui-sync-map-2026-10-23.md`, `files/control-base-phase1-plan-2026-10-23.md` (idea + Law 0), brain repo layout at `~/workspace/company/dream-brain/` (`core/`, `knowledge/`, `inbox/`, `scripts/`, `portal/`, `local-max/`) |
| 3 | `algorithms.md` | Algorithms and Methods | Brain repo scripts, read at generation time: `scripts/write-gate.mjs`, `scripts/surprise-v2.mjs`, `scripts/core-gravity.mjs`, `scripts/consolidate.mjs`, `scripts/calibration-tracker.mjs`, `scripts/boundary-probe.mjs`, `scripts/verdict-ledger.mjs`, `scripts/prediction-engine.mjs`, `scripts/graph-history.mjs`, `scripts/doorbell.mjs`, `scripts/window-pull.mjs`, `scripts/skill-admission.mjs`, `scripts/local-max-ask.mjs`, `scripts/promotion-gate.mjs`, `scripts/selfmod-guard.mjs`, `scripts/eval-gate.mjs`; portal sync reader `portal/vitals.js` + `window.__brainVitals` export in `portal/app.js` |
| 4 | `tech-stack.md` | Tech Stack | Brain repo tree (`~/workspace/company/dream-brain/`), `portal/` file inventory, `ops/RUNBOOK.md`, plan hard constraints (lightweight budgets) |
| 5 | `plan-and-gates.md` | Plan and Gates | `files/control-base-phase1-plan-2026-10-23.md` (WBS, schedule, gates, Addenda 2 and 3), `knowledge-base/REFERENCE.md` (dates) |
| 6 | `accomplishments.md` | Accomplishments | `dream-brain/knowledge/patterns/ops-log.md` (shipped increments with commits and tags), `knowledge-base/LOG.md`, `hidden_files/backlog.md` (scene completion entries) |
| 7 | `dictionary.md` | Dictionary | `files/THE-BOOKLET.md` Part 8 (project dictionary), `dream-brain/GLOSSARY.md` (system terms) |
| 8 | `log-feed.md` | Log Feed | `knowledge-base/LOG.md` and `dream-brain/knowledge/patterns/ops-log.md`, newest first; format contract defined in the file itself |

## Surfaces

- **Live (tailnet only):** all sections, plus live status values from
  `/api/live-state` and the SSE stream at `/api/stream`.
- **Public snapshot:** the professional subset (Overview, Architecture,
  Algorithms, Tech Stack, Plan and Gates, Accomplishments, Dictionary),
  labelled as a snapshot. No live values are published; counts shown are
  the snapshot counts at publish time.

## Bundle status

Generated 2026-10-23 (Fri) evening PT, ahead of the S-KB UI build, so the
UI work is pure wiring. Bundle version: v1.
